rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Each listed source carries a freshness STAMP, not just a to-do.
rules_evaluated.evidence: horthy-ace-fca's stamp reads `[checked:2026-07-31 result:CAVEAT due:asap]`. §11a's own grammar restricts `due:asap` to results in {CORRECT,GONE,NEEDED,STALE}; CAVEAT is not in that set. Its sibling stamp two lines above, huntley-context-window, carries the identical result (CAVEAT) and WAS fixed in the diff since pin 8cc00874 — from `due:asap` to a computed pub+6mo date (`due:2026-01-14`) — but the same fix was never applied to horthy-ace-fca (confirmed: `git diff 8cc00874..HEAD` touches the huntley-context-window line but not the horthy-ace-fca line). horthy-ace-fca's own prose names its true anchor ('last substantively edited 2025-12-03'); pub+6mo = 2026-06-03, three months overdue as of today (2026-09-05). Ran `bash curriculum/evals/scripts/source-freshness.sh --target 2026-09-05 curriculum/lectures/the-loop-half-filled.md` and read the script's own case logic (lines ~132-136): a CAVEAT whose due is a literal calendar date DOES escalate to WARN once past ('CAVEAT past its own due:... — re-verify or re-stamp', exactly what fires for huntley-context-window at L122), but a CAVEAT on due:asap is explicitly treated as a permanent exemption, same bucket as due:none/due:cohort ('A CAVEAT on due:none / due:cohort / due:asap keeps the exemption in full') and lands as plain 'accepted caveat' INFO. So the grammar slip is not cosmetic: it is the specific mechanism hiding this source's real 3-month staleness from the WARN list a pre-cohort audit reads for actionable debt — the exact harm §11a exists to prevent ('A bare verify-X rots... every cohort re-verifies from scratch').
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Replace `due:asap` with the computed `due:2026-06-03` on the horthy-ace-fca stamp, mirroring the fix already landed on huntley-context-window one line above it in the same Sources list.
